query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a secondary phase, such as a BCC phase, into the single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloy through composition modification can increase the coercive field.
generation.intervention: Composition modification to introduce a secondary BCC phase
generation.conditions: Alloy composition, processing conditions, and measurement techniques
generation.structural_mediator: Presence of a secondary BCC phase
generation.mechanism: Increased magnetic anisotropy and pinning of domain walls due to the secondary phase
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloy with a coercive field of less than 100 Oe
generation.boundary: Alloy composition, processing conditions, and measurement techniques
generation.uncertainty: The exact composition and processing conditions required to introduce a secondary BCC phase and increase the coercive field are uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of FeCoNi alloys with varying compositions and processing conditions to introduce a secondary BCC phase, and measure the coercive field using VSM or other techniques
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercive field does not increase with the introduction of a secondary BCC phase, the hypothesis is falsified

Own digest: Paper card. Question: How does the addition of Sn (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) affect the phase constitution, microstructure, and magnetic properties (specifically saturation magnetization, remanence, and Curie temperature) of FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 high-entropy alloys?. System: FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10). Processing: Vacuum arc-melting of 99.99% purity constituent elements using a water-cooled Cu crucible, followed by suction casting into a 100 × 10× 2 mm water-cooled Cu mold after remelting four times.. Test conditions: XRD scan speed of 1°/min; VSM measurements at an applied magnetic field of 1 T; HCTS hysteresis curves using a 27 × 9 × 1.7 mm rectangular sample at a magnetic field of 25 kA/m; DSC thermal stability analysis at a heating rate of 10 K/min.. Findings: The ratio of I(110)BCC/I(111)FCC increases from 0.38 (x=0) to 10.53 (x=0.10), indicating a rapid increase in BCC phase content.; Saturation magnetization (Ms) increases from 78.6 Am2/kg to 88.8 Am2/kg as x increases f
